paper.title: SEFRQO: A Self-Evolving Fine-Tuned RAG-Based Query Optimizer
paper.central_claim: SEFRQO, a fine-tuned LLM query-hint generator whose prompt is rebuilt each iteration from a continually updated vector DB of execution records (similar queries + the query's own best plan and gain), self-evolves from execution feedback and outperforms PostgreSQL, Bao and Balsa: up to 65.05% (CEB) and 93.57% (Stack) latency reduction vs PostgreSQL.

signatures.object: Per-query execution-record store (Milvus VecDB: SQL embedding, plan, execution time, iteration) and the dynamic user prompt of an inference-frozen LLM
signatures.information: SQL text, table cardinalities/selectivities from the engine, top-k similar queries' records (k=1..3), the query's own historical best plan and gain eta; actual latency of executed hints
signatures.operation: LLM emits a full-plan or join-order hint -> execute on PostgreSQL -> if faster than stored best, replace record -> recompute eta -> rebuild prompt for next iteration
signatures.output: hint (valid plan or fallback to default plan); updated record
signatures.conditions: queries repeated for 50 iterations; OLAP only; k small; invalid hints fall back to the default plan (homogeneous rate HR)
signatures.feedback: measured latency vs baseline latency stored at initialisation
signatures.selection_rule: strictly lower latency replaces the stored best (also a natural rollback to best-so-far)
signatures.selection_data: same executions that are later reported (per-query, 50 iterations)
signatures.persistence: VecDB entries survive across iterations and workloads
signatures.later_use: same query's next prompt; other queries via similarity retrieval
signatures.claimed_effect: CEB overall 60.04% (LS8B); Stack filtered 93.57%; dynamic mix 53.25%/69.98%
signatures.failure_boundary: data drift interference; noisy single-run latency; invalid/repeated hints; RL fine-tune variance; OLAP-only

signatures.object: Hint-generating LLM weights (LLaMA-3.1 3B/8B) - offline SFT then QGRPO (context, weight-touching)
signatures.information: SFT: (query+cardinalities) -> PostgreSQL's own hint; QGRPO: group-relative advantage of tanh(ln(baseline/latency)) over executed hints
signatures.operation: supervised imitation then RL with execution-latency reward on JOB
signatures.conditions: JOB as training workload; SFT prompts contain no retrieved references or best-plan feedback
signatures.claimed_effect: vanilla L3B/L8B give little gain; LS* strong; QGRPO mixed (hurts CEB, helps 3B on Stack)
signatures.failure_boundary: RL variance (LSG8B no better than LS8B)

gap.author_gap: Existing LQOs capture at most two of {learn from mistakes, no cold start, adapt to workload/schema change}; LLM optimizers cannot update cheaply at runtime.
gap.checked_gap: The runtime-learning gap for LLM optimizers is real, but 'no cold start' is not delivered by the evidence (first-iteration plans have higher RET; gains accrue over tens of repeated executions) and the per-query best-so-far memory is a repeated-execution search, not cross-query learning.
closest_adjacent: Bao, Balsa (trained 50 iterations on the same workload)
LLM-QO and LLMOpt not reproduced (no code)
gap.residue: Fixed-prompt LLM optimizers cannot incorporate execution feedback without retraining.
gap.stakes: Retraining on workload/schema shifts; latency of long OLAP queries.
gap.method_response: Rebuild the prompt from a vector DB of execution records plus own-best feedback; fine-tune once on JOB.
gap.remaining_gap: No held-out queries for the retained store; no comparison with plain best-of-N LLM sampling or random hint search at equal executions; Stack overall below Bao/Balsa.
unresolved: LLM-QO and LLMOpt originals unavailable in the pinned package; SERAG not read

assessment.evidence_level_note: Retained records are written and re-read on the same repeated queries that are scored, and Table 1 is best-of-50 per query (opus:O03): selection set = test set → at most task (EVIDENCE rule 2). JOB→Stack transfer certifies the fine-tuned weights, not the VecDB.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported single runs: a JOB-fine-tuned LLaMA hint generator whose prompt is rebuilt from execution records lowers best-found CEB latency by ~50–60% overall vs PostgreSQL when each query is executed 50 times; similar-query references add ~9 points overall (NR). Not shown: gains beyond equal-execution resampling, QGRPO benefit, superiority over Bao/Balsa on Stack overall (40.10 vs 67.17/76.90).
unresolved: No feedback-off control at equal execution count.
